subject.title: feat(secrets): egress-time credential injection with process-local sentinels

question: Should this PR proceed with the process-local sentinel design after the local-service probe is made sentinel-safe, or should maintainers require a narrower staged hardening plan first?
rationale: The linked issue is source-supported and this PR is a plausible core security fix, but it changes cross-cutting credential handling and currently leaves one concrete pre-guarded egress path.

options.title: Fix probe boundary and continue
options.body: Require the local-service health-probe path to preserve sentinels or unwrap only inside a guarded egress helper, then continue reviewing this PR as the canonical fix.

options.title: Stage a smaller hardening PR
options.body: Ask for exact-value redaction and guarded-fetch convergence first, leaving full sentinels until provider and local-service semantics are approved.

options.title: Keep the current process boundary
options.body: Do not merge this sentinel approach now and keep the documented same-process plaintext limitation until a broader broker or plugin API design exists.

recommendation.title: Fix probe boundary and continue
recommendation.body: Require the local-service health-probe path to preserve sentinels or unwrap only inside a guarded egress helper, then continue reviewing this PR as the canonical fix.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current history on SecretRef and auth-profile resolution, which is the first security boundary this decision changes.
